answer: An agent economy can make reputation depend on a long-lived stake rather than on account age alone: each agent locks tokens that are slashed if it is caught coordinating fake identities to claim rewards. To gain influence, a sybil operator must split capital among identities and keep it locked while those identities build credible histories; recycling one stake across accounts is prevented by the lock. A raven may expose a hollow cluster with an opal-bright reward pattern, but the defense is the costly bond: attack requires real capital at risk for as long as the deception must persist.
